strategy.summary: Reproduce the einsum precision regression by building NumPy at the buggy commit 031a8906a576 and running the developer's test test_einsum_chunking_precision, which sums 1,000,000 broadcast float64 values and asserts agreement to decimal=15. The defect lives in the C einsum path (einsum.c.src, PyArray_EinsteinSum), so the test only transitions after a source build of the buggy and fixed revisions. The PR removes NPY_ITER_GROWINNER from iter_flags.

strategy.reproducing_test: numpy/_core/tests/test_einsum.py::test_einsum_chunking_precision: num = 1_000_000; value = 1. + np.finfo(np.float64).eps * 8196; res = np.einsum('i->', np.broadcast_to(np.array(value), num)) / num; assert_almost_equal(res, value, decimal=15)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 031a8906a576 the test FAILS: the reduction with GROWINNER active gives a result whose deviation from value exceeds the decimal=15 tolerance, so assert_almost_equal raises AssertionError. On the fixed revision, with NPY_ITER_GROWINNER removed from iter_flags, the same test PASSES. The transition is the success criterion; no printed values are checked.
strategy.numerical_probe: Run the same expression at buggy and fixed revisions and compare abs(res - value) against 1.5e-15; the test itself is the authoritative check.
risks: The buggy-side failure is inferred from the PR and test design, not from an observed value in the evidence; if the buggy build does not exceed decimal=15 at num=1_000_000 on the target platform, the test will not transition and the mechanism cannot be confirmed here.

Whether GROWINNER is active depends on nditer buffer and chunk sizes, which the evidence does not give numerically; the outcome may depend on the NumPy build's default buffersize and on whether the reduction takes the buffered path.

The developer's test sizes the array at 1,000,000 elements, while the expected_behavior text cites 100000000 with np.full; the reproduction follows the test diff, which is the authoritative artefact. The 100,000,000-element case is impractical and is not planned.

The test docstring says 'At with GROWINNER 11 decimals succeed' while the assertion uses decimal=15; the threshold is therefore internally inconsistent in the evidence, and decimal=15 is treated as the separation threshold per the test code.

The precision guarantee is explicitly described as unclear, so the transition may be sensitive to platform floating-point behaviour, SIMD code paths and compiler optimisation flags, which the evidence does not specify. A failure seen only on one architecture or with one compiler will not transition elsewhere.

The build requires a C compiler and the NumPy meson build toolchain; the evidence does not list these, so they must be supplied by the environment.

oracle.reference_source: test_einsum_chunking_precision assertion in the developer's test diff
oracle.why: The test compares the mean of 1,000,000 identical float64 values against the exact value, so any accumulated rounding error shows up directly in the mean; decimal=15 is the threshold the test encodes.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The assertion sees res differing from value by more than 1.5e-15 on the buggy revision (GROWINNER active, unchunked accumulation loses precision), so assert_almost_equal raises AssertionError. This is inferred from the PR design; the observed buggy value is not given in the evidence.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With NPY_ITER_GROWINNER removed from iter_flags, the reduction is chunked at the buffer size, the accumulated error stays within decimal=15 of value, and assert_almost_equal passes.
